quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: What does a red curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
A place to pick up or drop off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams bounce back and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate traffic lanes, passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the left.
Allowed from the right.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean about passing?

options.text: Do not pass until after you pass the sign.
Do not pass unless it seems safe.
Do not pass for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass for any reason.
questions.explanation: A white sign means you must obey the rule. This sign means never pass other vehicles.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the rest of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than the rest of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Speeding increases collision risk. Driving too slowly can cause rear-end crashes or make other drivers swerve.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane can pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite traffic directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to other vehicles to keep traction.
Pump your brakes to prevent them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going down steep hills to prevent skidding. Keep more distance from other vehicles. Avoid quick stops. Pump brakes if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Always consider the situation. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming cars or people and could cause a crash.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. When parked uphill or downhill, angle your wheels so your car won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even shallow water can hide dangers. If you find flooding, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you of a school zone or school crossing. When you see these signs, stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a side road intersection is ahead.

questions.question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:

options.text: Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: If a car is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating, merge into another lane if possible. If you cannot merge, slowly reduce your speed when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: If you must park in an unusual location, you should:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers from any direction.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers from any direction.
questions.explanation: You are responsible for making sure your parked car is not a hazard. Park where drivers can see your car from any direction.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The highest speed allowed is 55 mph in good conditions.
You cannot drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest speed allowed is 55 mph in good conditions.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs tell you the maximum speed allowed. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
Traffic is merging ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid accidents and brake damage.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Look in the side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. You must look over your shoulder to see the blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Drivers in both directions may pass.
Drivers on the broken line side may pass.
Drivers on the solid line side may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers on the broken line side may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass on that side.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait for the light to change.
Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the right lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you turn in that direction if you are in the correct lane. Make sure the intersection is clear and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles before turning.
